        "id": "Q01",
        "topics": [
          "scenario",

        "question": "它给谁提供什么可验收交付，贡献在哪里？",
        "answer": "面向需要通用网页和社媒资料、又不想分别维护多套Agent工具的人。它注册ctx.web搜索/抓取Provider，沿DSH标准web_search/web_fetch交付URL、标题、片段或文本；8类内置通用源、可声明式自定义源、X/小红书专用浏览器来源共同在一条接口下服务。原基线为单Provider或手工切换接口。合格交付应能确认实际后端、检索方式、时间/范围、错误及截断，而非只看工具成功或片段很多。\n\n核心贡献是SearchHints到原生参数的适配、多Key/Provider健康与fallback、配置面凭证/出站策略及平台来源接线，减少“所有源仅共同最小能力”的取舍。它不是自建搜索引擎，也不认证网页事实或平台评论代表性。普通检索与原生站内/评论具有不同证据等级，不能因统一返回字符串就互相替代。发布版最外层还会丢部分backend/retrievalMode/truncated，后文说明其保证被收窄。",

        "id": "Q02",

        "question": "语义编译和容灾具体如何工作，有什么损失？",
        "answer": "SearchHints是确定性正则/词表，不是语义模型推理。抽site/-site、平台前缀、after/before、主题、freshness和显式国家，中文语言不直接等中国、global/多国抑制单国偏置。Tavily将news/finance、日期/域名/国家编原生字段，Exa将research→publication和发布日范围，SearXNG映categories/time_range/language，各源支持范围不同。优点是意图结构复用，限制是词法歧义、日期合法性/跨语境与字段未支持时的退化，需核实际结果，不能称完整保义编译。\n\n搜索有ordered/round-robin/random候选链；每Provider按健康key的inFlight、uses、固定顺序选，reserve/finally release共享search/fetch池，auth失败才同源换Key；429/网络/超时/5xx转下一源，Retry-After冷却避免无效请求。auth坏Key留不健康直到凭证实际变化，不是每次全池自动reset，pool模块旧注释不可替执行器语义。未知错误code默认retryable，只有bad-request/config停链、aborted终止，可能将未知协议错误变成多源开销。fetch只取一个健康Key，auth失败转下一Provider，不同于search同源循环；非重试fetch错误break native循环后仍可generic fallback。每尝试signal超时但需adapter实际受理abort，整个链总时延/费用仍受链长和宿主工具预算约束。",

        "question": "关闭/始终联网可以理解成什么保证？",
        "answer": "每session mode存在内存，turn开始冻结required/disabled用于提示和结束判断；Agent自己scope注册listeners，off时限制可见工具并monotonic guard拒web_search/web_fetch，首次step注入说明，unload撤监听和限制。相比仅提示不联网，是针对这两个工具名的运行前守卫。它不能阻止shell/curl、其他网络工具、模型服务或设置页的测试/额度/版本请求，也不会因为off就关闭已有CDP/浏览器，故README“绝不产生外部网络请求/物理隔离”超出本层范围。\n\nrequired的完成条件是任意search或fetch工具result事件，不管isError是否成功；success另存但停止判定只看completed。失败已返回也可结束，符合“失败说明未知”的降级，不等每轮已取得有效外部权威依据。若没调则一次steer纠正，再停止则cancel；不能保证相关性、引用质量或证据充分。mode中途变化时liveguard/restriction读当前off，冻结required提示/turn记录却仍旧，需要向读者区分“当前工具禁止”与“本轮完成目标”。普通mode不经磁盘保存，session重建依默认auto。",

        "question": "通用fetch安全链和结果完整性是否闭合？",
        "answer": "generic fetch只允许HTTP(S)、拒userinfo与私网/本地/metadata，预查所有DNS地址，最多5跳手工redirect每跳重验，正文stream5MiB上限、MIME排除二进制/PDF，HTML用linkedom+Defuddle useAsync=false本地提取，失败可保raw。这些防护和截断都有具体实现，但本地解析不等网络不外发，抓取仍请求目标/代理，模型也接文本。\n\nDNS预查函数返回void，generic随后调用fetchWithProxy不带provider模式；fetch-proxy的page/legacy路径普通fetch/ProxyAgent重新解析，严格pinned dispatcher只用于非官方provider覆盖路径。故通用页面“预查即防rebind”不闭合，检查与连接可不同DNS/代理端解析，未复现攻击但不能外推为锁定IP。native第三方fetch先把URL交Provider，通用页URL过滤也不是第三方内部取URL行为的本地全程管控。\n\n完整性投影有确定丢失。generic返回finalUrl/status/truncated/backend/metadata；sources.registry的general分支只把部分字段放item，丢truncated/status/backend，toRoutedFetchResponse再硬置输入url、200和truncated=false，最终工具可能把5MiB裁剪内容表示未截断，redirect最终URL也丢。搜索外包装同样只留sources与false，不暴露attempts/backend/retrievalMode。平台评论的captured/truncated仍嵌在正文，是局部保留，不能补所有抓取完整性。读者应另核原网页，不把成功text当全文。",

        "question": "自定义源与凭证的正向设计和边界是什么？",
        "answer": "自定义三类协议只做数据模板/点路径映射，无eval；单次placeholder替换避免query中的{{apiKey}}二次展开，mapping拒prototype相关段且只走own property。Basic账号密码分credential refs，key不回显配置；自定义search-only不假设兼容extract。transport区分模型选的网页和操作者配置的端点，host/port授权、HTTP/private确认、metadata/linklocal硬阻断、DNS所有候选检查、direct socket pinning、redirect:error、JSON响应2MiB预算与reserved headers限制，具备可借鉴的出站安全分层。代理最终解析不可本地证明，需allowProxy明确授权，而不是宣称代理链同样本地pin住。\n\n配置面以真实loopback TCP peer+sameOrigin/sec-fetch-site而非仅Host，有真实peer时优先核loopback，缺peer时只有NODE_ENV=test或任一argv/execArgv包含test子串才退化为Host判断；否则failclosed。这个字符串条件不是可信自动测试证明，普通带test字样进程也可命中；但不改变有peer的优先检查，不能据此声称真实TCP对端已绕过。它是本机配置面信任模型，反代变本地peer或其他本机进程仍需宿主认证，非多租户用户身份隔离。create先写配置再写凭证，失败补偿恢复/撤secret，update需revision并有补偿；但revision比较在异步DNS/write前完成，无原子CAS/串行锁，双请求可同时通过旧revision。补偿失败catch忽略也不等事务回滚保证。DNS preflight在combineAbort创建前等待lookup，不受后面requestTimeout直接中断；外层attempt信号能否及时结束依链中等待点，不能把15秒配置当所有DNS绝对上限。",

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "<div align=\"center\">\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools/main/assets/logo.png\" alt=\"dsh-web-tools\" width=\"160\" />\n</p>\n\n# dsh-web-tools\n\nEmpower DeepSeek Harness with unified search and deep content extraction across the open web and social platforms.\n\n**Native-Capability Adaptation Across 8 Web Providers · SearchHints Semantic Compilation · Multi-Source Resilience · Xiaohongshu & Twitter / X Retrieval**\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools/stargazers\">\n    <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/github/stars/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools?style=flat-square&label=Stars\" alt=\"GitHub Stars\" />\n  </a>\n  <a href=\"LICENSE\">\n    <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-2ea44f?style=flat-square\" alt=\"MIT License\" />\n  </a>\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness\">\n    <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-Web%20Runtime-4D6BFE?style=flat-square\" alt=\"DeepSeek Harness\" />\n  </a>\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.x-3178C6?style=flat-square&logo=typescript&logoColor=white\" alt=\"TypeScript\" />\n</p>\n\n**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)\n\n</div>\n\n## What problem does it solve?\n\nWhen web access depends on a single provider, exhausted quota, rate limits, or timeouts can interrupt retrieval. Wrapping multiple APIs with a naive proxy often flattens them to a lowest common denominator, failing to leverage each provider's specialized search modes, categories, freshness, domain rules, and extraction capabilities.\n\ndsh-web-tools connects Exa, Tavily, Firecrawl, Parallel, Brave, You.com, Jina, SearXNG, Xiaohongshu, and Twitter / X to DSH’s standard `web_search` / `web_fetch` interface.\n\nWhile keeping the tool interface unified, dsh-web-tools normalizes search intents through SearchHints and compiles queries into native provider-specific parameters. This leverages each engine's native categories, freshness filters, domain policies, regional targeting, and content extraction, while maximizing uptime through multi-key allocation, automated failover, and dedicated browser profiles.\n\n---\n\n**Key Highlights**:\n\n- **Native-Capability Adaptation Across 8 Web Providers**: Keeps the standard `web_search` / `web_fetch` contracts while compiling unified search intent into provider-specific native parameters instead of reducing every backend to the same lowest-common-denominator feature set.\n- **SearchHints → Provider-Specific Parameter Compilation**: Normalizes technical, research, news, date, region, and domain constraints from queries, compiling them into provider-native parameters through deterministic code without additional LLM latency.\n- **Xiaohongshu & Twitter / X Platform Sources**: Both platforms support signed-in native search, detail extraction, and returned comments or replies through dedicated local browser profiles.\n- **Multi-Source Scheduling & Resilience**: Features multi-API-key pooling, 401 failover, 429 cooldown windows, configurable Ordered / Round-Robin / Random routing, and failover chains.\n- **Native DSH Tool Integration**: Plugs directly into standard `web_search` / `web_fetch` without requiring new tool declarations, and includes a session-level \"Search Mode\" toggle.\n\n```text\n                         DSH Agent\n                            │\n                 web_search / web_fetch\n                            │\n                            ▼\n                       SearchHints\n            topic / freshness / domains\n               locale / cleanQuery ...\n                            │\n                 Provider-specific\n                    compilation\n                            │\n      ┌────────┬─────────┬───────────┬──────────┐\n      │  Exa   │ Tavily  │ Firecrawl │ Parallel │ ...\n      │        │         │           │          │\n      │category│ topic   │ github    │objective │\n      │ date   │ chunks  │ research  │ policy   │\n      │domains │ time    │ tbs       │ queries  │\n      └────────┴─────────┴───────────┴──────────┘\n\n```\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools/main/assets/searchOrderAndRouting.png\" width=\"900\" alt=\"dsh-web-tools search strategy and multi-provider routing\" />\n</p>\n\n## Native-Capability Adaptation Across 8 Web Providers\n\nThe tool interface and search semantics are unified for the DSH agent, but underlying provider capabilities are not.\n\ndsh-web-tools expresses query intent through SearchHints and crafts dedicated requests for each provider, rather than compressing all backends into a single set of lowest-common-denominator parameters.\n\nFor example, when searching for \"AI coding references from the past week\":\n\n* **Exa**: Maps category filters, ISO date ranges, and domain constraints;\n* **Firecrawl**: Maps technical queries to the native `github` category, research queries to `research`, and applies `tbs` freshness filters;\n* **Parallel**: Deconstructs the query into `objective`, clean `search_queries`, and `source_policy`;\n* **Brave Search**: Maps freshness, country, and language parameters with priority LLM Context endpoint;\n* **You.com**: Leverages `boost_domains` for soft domain preference.\n\nAll adaptations run through deterministic code without invoking an extra LLM call.\n\n* **Exa**: Category mapping (`publication` / `news` / `financial report`), ISO-8601 date ranges, and domain constraints.\n* **Firecrawl**: Maps coding and technical queries to the `github` category, academic queries to `research`, and supports `tbs`, domain constraints, and clean Markdown extraction.\n* **Parallel**: Dual-layer semantics (`objective` soft-steering + clean `search_queries`) and `source_policy` domain/freshness filters.\n* **Tavily**: Supports `basic` / `advanced` / `fast` / `ultra-fast` search depths; `basic`, `advanced`, and `fast` support `chunks_per_source`, with native `news` / `finance` topics, date ranges, country, and domain constraints.\n* **Brave Search**: LLM Context endpoint with `pd/pw/pm/py` freshness filters, country, and search language.\n* **You.com**: Native **`boost_domains`** soft-weighting, freshness presets, and geo/language targeting.\n* **Jina**: Query noise reduction and ReaderLM-v2 high-precision markdown extraction.\n* **SearXNG**: Self-hosted metasearch with `categories` (it/science/news) and `time_range`.\n* **Native & Generic Page Extraction (`web_fetch`)**: Automatically routes to provider-native scraping backends (Exa `/contents`, Tavily `/extract`, Firecrawl `/scrape`, Parallel `/v1/extract`, You.com `/v1/contents`, Jina Reader) when available; seamlessly falls back to the **built-in generic HTTP fetcher** (powered by local Defuddle Markdown parsing with SSRF/DNS protection) for SearXNG-only / Brave-only setups or when native extractors fail.\n\n---\n\n## Social Platform Sources\n\nUnlike general search engines, the plugin connects directly to native social platform sessions:\n\n* **Native Isolated Browser Architecture**:\n  * Directly controls local Edge / Chrome instances using dedicated profiles over CDP.\n  * **0 browser extensions and 0 Playwright / Chromium bundles**. Cookies remain managed by the dedicated browser profile and are not written to plugin configuration, logs, or relays; the browser still sends them to the platform during normal authenticated requests.\n\n* **Xiaohongshu**:\n  * **Note Detail & Comment Fetch (`web_fetch`)**: Uses the dedicated browser profile to extract structured `__INITIAL_STATE__` data with DOM fallback while preserving signed `xsec_token` URLs. When the page loads comment data, top-level comments and returned nested replies are extracted individually.\n  * **Native Search Discovery (`web_search`)**: Uses the signed-in browser and the real search controls on `/explore`, entering only the cleaned topic query rather than platform names or `site:` operators. It distinguishes login walls, security verification, and a genuinely signed-out session. Operators can temporarily disable this path with `XHS_NATIVE_SEARCH=0` while diagnosing browser issues.\n\n* **Twitter / X**:\n  * **Native Search, Tweet Detail & Replies**: Captures the X web client's GraphQL data streams (SearchTimeline / TweetDetail) over CDP, parses the target tweet and its reply tree structurally, and uses DOM extraction as a supplement and fallback. Supports `from:`, `since:`, and `until:` operators.\n\nEach detail fetch includes at most 30 comments or replies, with up to 800 characters per entry. Additional pages or nested replies are explicitly marked as truncated to keep model context bounded.\n\n> **Capability Boundary**: For Xiaohongshu notes where the primary content resides in images, the fetcher returns the title, text description, engagement metrics, image count, and loaded comments; it does not perform optical character recognition (OCR) on image text or automatically paginate through all comments.\n\nAgents use `小红书:` or `X:` as a platform-routing prefix. The prefix selects the platform and is removed before the native search runs; for example, `小红书: DeepSeek Harness` enters only `DeepSeek Harness` into Xiaohongshu's search box.\n\n* **General-Web Fallback**: Uses configured general search or fetch providers when a platform source is disabled, temporarily unavailable, or reports a retryable failure. Non-retryable sign-in, access-control, search-restriction, and invalid-detail errors are returned directly so indexed content is not presented as native platform results, details, or comments.\n* **Automated Session Verification**: Cookies are only the first gate. Xiaohongshu requires both `a1` and `web_session`, then performs a stabilized live `/explore` check in the interactive browser. A visible login wall invalidates the old session and restores the sign-in action; a wall appearing only after search submission is reported directly as `search-restricted` rather than being hidden behind indexed web results.\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools/main/assets/platformSessions.png\" width=\"900\" alt=\"Xiaohongshu and Twitter X signed-in sessions verified automatically\" />\n</p>\n\n---\n\n## Custom Search Providers & Address Overrides (Issue #9)\n\nIn addition to the 8 built-in search adapters and social platforms, dsh-web-tools natively supports **Custom Search Providers** and **Built-in Service Address Overrides**:\n\n* **Built-in Base URL Overrides**:\n  * All 8 built-in search providers (Exa, Tavily, Firecrawl, Brave, You, Parallel, Jina, SearXNG) support custom service addresses (e.g. self-hosted API gateways, reverse proxies).\n  * Preserves path prefixes (such as `/v1`, `/v2`), prompts for confirmation on foreign destinations to protect API keys, and supports instant restoration to official defaults.\n* **Three Parallel Access Paths (Progressive Modal UX)**:\n  * **Compatible Provider API**: Follows the standard Tavily POST JSON specification with zero manual mapping. Ideal for self-hosted proxies and compatible gateways.\n  * **Protocol Template**: Pre-configured standard meta-search protocol (e.g. SearXNG JSON `GET /search?format=json`), keyless by default with automatic result mapping.\n  * **Custom JSON API (Generic JSON)**: Full declarative mapping engine for internal knowledge bases, private clusters, or arbitrary RESTful search endpoints:\n    * **Custom Request Headers**: Add arbitrary HTTP headers with `{{apiKey}}` and `{{query}}` placeholder interpolation.\n    * **Nested JSON Body Template (`bodyTemplate`)**: In POST JSON mode, author arbitrary nested JSON request bodies (e.g. `{\"query\": \"{{query}}\", \"limit\": \"{{maxResults}}\"}`) without writing code.\n    * **Query Parameters Template (`paramsTemplate`)**: In GET or query-encoded mode, configure custom query parameters with full placeholder support.\n    * **Declarative Response Mapping**: Non-executable dot-path reader (`itemsPath`, `urlPath`, `titlePath`, `snippetPath`, etc.) with prototype pollution defenses.\n    * **Single-Pass Interpolation**: Prevents recursive placeholder expansion and secret leakage when user query contains placeholder syntax.\n    * **Real-Time Syntax Validation**: Invalid JSON in the body template immediately triggers visual error feedback and disables testing/saving to prevent stale config writes.\n* **Credential Isolation & Key Pooling**:\n  * Supports Bearer Token, API Key Header, HTTP Basic (isolated username/password storage with rollback compensation), and Keyless modes.\n  * API secrets are managed securely by the DSH credentials service and never echoed back to browser configuration views. Integrates with key rotation and health tracking.\n* **Draft Testing & Routing Integration**:\n  * Test search drafts directly before saving to verify latency and field mapping without contaminating runtime health or circuit breakers.\n  * Custom providers seamlessly participate in fallback chains and routing policies (Ordered, Round-Robin, Random).\n* **Tiered Outbound Security & SSRF Defense**:\n  * **Default Safe Destinations**: Public HTTPS targets and default self-hosted SearXNG (`127.0.0.1:8080`, `localhost:8080`) are pre-authorized with zero dialogs.\n  * **Explicit Operator Confirmation (409 Conflict)**: Private RFC 1918 networks, plain unencrypted HTTP, and custom domains resolving to private IPs (probed via `resolvesToPrivateIp()`) require explicit one-time confirmation before issuing outbound grants. Silent auto-authorization is strictly prohibited.\n  * **Shared Endpoint Lifecycle Cleanup**: Managed authorizations (`managedBy: \"custom-source\"`) are safely reused when multiple custom sources share an internal endpoint, and automatically revoked when the last source is deleted or reassigned. System defaults remain untouched.\n  * **Unconditional Cloud Metadata & Link-Local Hard Blocks**: `169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10` (fe80:: to febf::), IPv4-mapped variants (`::ffff:a9fe:a9fe`, etc.), and IMDSv6 are unconditionally blocked at the transport layer, even if explicitly authorized.\n  * **Proxy Egress & Pinned Connections**: Public custom endpoints automatically route through `undici.ProxyAgent` when a Windows system proxy or `HTTP_PROXY` is configured; private and loopback targets strictly bypass the proxy and dial directly with IP pinning.\n  * **Configuration Plane Integrity**: Privileged management routes verify genuine TCP socket `remoteAddress` to prevent Host header spoofing.\n\n---\n\n## Fallback & Resilience\n\n* **Multi-API-Key Pooling**: Assigns keys per provider, balances concurrent requests by lowest in-flight count, and fails over across keys on authentication errors.\n* **Deterministic Provider Fallback**: Automatically cascades through the fallback chain on network failures, timeouts, 5xx server errors, 429 rate limits, or exhausted quotas.\n* **429 Retry-After Cooldown**: Enforces zero-request cooldown windows when servers return `Retry-After` headers, skipping rate-limited providers immediately.\n* **Configurable Routing Policies**: `web_search` supports Ordered, Round-Robin, and Random starting-provider selection. `web_fetch` always follows the deterministic fetch-capable chain.\n* **Session-Level Search Mode**: A refined, compact picker in the composer offering three deterministic retrieval behaviors (defaults to Smart):\n  * **Smart (智能联网)**: Elastic semantic dispatch. The agent autonomously determines whether real-time web retrieval is needed based on conversational intent.\n  * **Always (始终联网)**: Strong-consistency knowledge verification. Mandates at least one completed `web_search` or `web_fetch` per turn to ensure claims are grounded in external sources.\n  * **Off (关闭联网)**: Deterministic physical isolation. Replaces fragile prompt-only requests with a **three-tier runtime enforcement barrier** (dynamically withholds tools from the agent's schema, blocks model inertia via a monotonic guard before execution, and injects a single-turn explanation), ensuring zero outbound network leakage regardless of historical context.\n\n<div align=\"center\">\n  <table>\n    <thead>\n      <tr>\n        <th align=\"center\">Dropdown Picker Menu</th>\n        <th align=\"center\">Active Trigger States</th>\n      </tr>\n    </thead>\n    <tbody>\n      <tr>\n        <td align=\"center\" width=\"55%\">\n          <img src=\"assets/search-mode-menu.png\" width=\"290\" alt=\"Search Mode Picker Menu\" />\n        </td>\n        <td align=\"center\" width=\"45%\">\n          <img src=\"assets/search-mode-smart.png\" height=\"28\" alt=\"Smart Mode\" /><br/>\n          <sub><b>Smart</b>: Adaptive autonomous dispatch (Default)</sub><br/><br/>\n          <img src=\"assets/search-mode-always.png\" height=\"28\" alt=\"Always Mode\" /><br/>\n          <sub><b>Always</b>: Enforced verification highlight</sub><br/><br/>\n          <img src=\"assets/search-mode-off.png\" height=\"28\" alt=\"Off Mode\" /><br/>\n          <sub><b>Off</b>: Runtime physical guard</sub>\n        </td>\n      </tr>\n    </tbody>\n  </table>\n</div>\n\n* **Intelligent Proxy Routing & Intranet Bypass**: Seamlessly integrates with Windows system proxy settings and `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` environment variables. />\n</p>\n\n# dsh-web-tools\n\n让 DeepSeek Harness 拥有直连全网与社媒平台的搜索与抓取能力。\n\n**8 大 Web Provider 原生能力适配 · SearchHints 语义编译 · 多源自动容灾 · 小红书 / Twitter X 平台检索**\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools/stargazers\">\n    <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/github/stars/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools?style=flat-square&label=Stars\" alt=\"GitHub Stars\" />\n  </a>\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.x-3178C6?style=flat-square&logo=typescript&logoColor=white\" alt=\"TypeScript\" />\n</p>\n\n[English](README.md) | **简体中文**\n\n</div>\n\n## 它解决什么问题\n\n当联网能力只依赖一个 Web Provider 时，额度耗尽、限流或服务异常都可能直接中断检索；而简单接入多个搜索 API，往往又只能使用它们共同支持的基础能力，没有真正发挥不同搜索源各自擅长的搜索模式、分类、时效、域名策略和正文提取能力。\n\ndsh-web-tools 将 Exa、Tavily、Firecrawl、Parallel、Brave、You.com、Jina、SearXNG，以及小红书、Twitter / X 接入 DSH 标准 `web_search` / `web_fetch`。\n\n在统一 DSH 工具接口的同时，dsh-web-tools 通过 SearchHints 归一化查询意图，再针对不同 Provider 分别编译为其支持的原生参数，尽可能使用各家的分类、时效、域名、地区、深度搜索与正文提取能力；同时通过多 API Key、Provider Fallback 和平台专用浏览器会话，提高整个联网链路的可用性。\n\n---\n\n**核心亮点**：\n\n- **8 大 Web Provider 原生能力深度适配**：保持统一 `web_search` / `web_fetch` 接口，但不把不同搜索源压成最低公共能力。针对 Exa、Tavily、Firecrawl、Parallel、Brave、You.com、Jina、SearXNG 分别适配搜索类型、时效、域名策略、地区语言、深度检索与正文提取能力。\n- **SearchHints → Provider-specific 参数编译**：将 Query 中的技术 / 论文 / 新闻、时效、域名、地区与语言等搜索意图归一化，再按不同 Provider 的能力映射为各自原生参数；整个过程由确定性代码完成，不增加额外 LLM 调用。\n- **小红书与 Twitter / X 平台来源**：两个平台均通过独立的本地浏览器 Profile 提供已登录站内搜索、详情抓取，以及页面实际返回的评论或回复。\n- **多搜索源调度与自动容灾**：支持多 API Key 分配、鉴权失败切换、429 冷却、Ordered / Round-Robin / Random 路由，以及可配置 Provider Fallback。\n- **DSH 原生工具集成**：直接复用标准 `web_search` / `web_fetch`，模型侧无需学习额外工具，同时提供会话级「联网搜索」模式。\n\n```text\n                         DSH Agent\n                            │\n                 web_search / web_fetch\n                            │\n                            ▼\n                       SearchHints\n            topic / freshness / domains\n               locale / cleanQuery ...\n                            │\n                 Provider-specific\n                    compilation\n                            │\n      ┌────────┬─────────┬───────────┬──────────┐\n      │  Exa   │ Tavily  │ Firecrawl │ Parallel │ ...\n      │        │         │           │          │\n      │category│ topic   │ github    │objective │\n      │ date   │ chunks  │ research  │ policy   │\n      │domains │ time    │ tbs       │ queries  │\n      └────────┴─────────┴───────────┴──────────┘\n\n```\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A3Boy/dsh-web-tools/main/assets/searchOrderAndRouting.png\" width=\"900\" alt=\"dsh-web-tools 搜索策略与多源调度\" />\n</p>\n\n## 8 大 Web Provider 原生能力深度适配\n\n统一的是 DSH 的工具接口和搜索语义，不统一的是各家 Provider 的能力。\n\ndsh-web-tools 通过 SearchHints 表达查询意图，再针对不同 Provider 分别构造请求，而不是把所有搜索源压缩成一套最低公共参数。\n\n例如，同样是“搜索最近一周的 AI 编程资料”：\n\n* **Exa**：映射分类、ISO 日期范围与域名限制；\n* **Firecrawl**：技术查询映射至 `github` 分类，研究类查询映射至 `research`，并结合 `tbs` 时效过滤；\n* **Parallel**：组合 `objective`、`search_queries` 与 `source_policy`；\n* **Brave Search**：映射 freshness、国家与搜索语言，并优先使用 LLM Context；\n* **You.com**：通过 `boost_domains` 对指定域名进行软加权。\n\n这些适配全部由确定性代码完成，不会为了选择 Provider 参数再额外调用一次 LLM。\n\n* **Exa**：精确分类映射（publication / news / financial report）、ISO 日期范围与域名限制。\n* **Firecrawl**：代码与技术查询映射至 `github` 分类，论文与学术查询映射至 `research`，并支持 `tbs` 时效、域名限制与 Clean Markdown 抓取。\n* **Parallel**：双层语义优化（`objective` 软引导 + `search_queries` 纯净词）与 `source_policy` 域名/时效过滤。\n* **Tavily**：支持 `basic` / `advanced` / `fast` / `ultra-fast` 搜索深度；`basic`、`advanced`、`fast` 模式支持 `chunks_per_source` 分块控制，并映射 `news` / `finance` 话题、日期区间、国家与域名约束。\n* **Brave Search**：LLM Context 预提取端点，支持 `pd/pw/pm/py` 时效、国家与搜索语言。\n* **You.com**：原生 **`boost_domains`** 软加权支持，时效与地区国家过滤。\n* **Jina**：搜索关键词降噪与 ReaderLM-v2 高精度 Markdown 正文解析。\n* **SearXNG**：自建元搜索支持 `categories` (it/science/news) 与 `time_range`。\n* **原生与通用正文提取 (`web_fetch`)**：配置 Tavily、Exa、Firecrawl、Parallel、You.com、Jina 时自动优先调用其原生云端提取接口；未配置或失败时，以及使用 SearXNG / Brave 时，自动平滑回退至**插件内置通用 HTTP 抓取器**（基于 Defuddle 纯本地 Markdown 解析与 SSRF / DNS 安全防护），无需额外配置或购买第三方 Fetch Key。\n\n---\n\n## 平台搜索源（小红书与 Twitter / X）\n\n区别于通用搜索引擎，插件通过专用浏览器会话直接连接社媒平台：\n\n* **原生独立浏览器会话架构**：\n  * 基于本机已安装的 Edge / Chrome 专用 Profile 与 CDP 通信。\n  * **0 浏览器扩展、0 Playwright / Chromium 外部打包**。Cookie 由专用浏览器 Profile 管理，插件不会将其写入配置、日志或中转服务；浏览器仍会按正常认证流程发送给对应平台。\n\n* **小红书**：\n  * **笔记详情与评论抓取 (`web_fetch`)**：通过专用浏览器 Profile 解析 `__INITIAL_STATE__` 结构化数据并自动 DOM 兜底，保留完整 `xsec_token` 签名 条评论或回复，单条内容最多保留 800 个字符；仍有后续分页或楼中楼内容时会明确标记为截断，避免无界占用模型上下文。\n\n> **能力边界说明**：对于正文主要位于图片中的小红书笔记，目前会返回标题、文字描述、互动数据、图片数量以及页面已加载的评论，但暂不识别图片中的文字，也不会自动抓取全部评论分页。\n\nAgent 使用 `小红书:` 或 `X:` 作为平台路由前缀。前缀只负责选择平台，插件会在实际站内搜索前移除它；例如 `小红书: DeepSeek Harness` 最终输入小红书搜索框的是 `DeepSeek Harness`。\n\n* **通用 Web 降级 (Web Fallback)**：平台来源未启用、运行时暂不可用或发生可重试故障时，改由已配置的通用搜索或抓取 Provider 处理；登录失效、访问受限、站内搜索受限、无效详情地址等非重试错误会直接返回，不会用索引内容冒充原生站内结果、详情或评论。\n* **登录态自动验证**：Cookie 只作为第一层门槛。小红书要求同时存在 `a1` 与 `web_session`，随后还会通过交互浏览器稳定检查 `/explore` 的真实页面状态；可见登录墙会使旧 Session The seam's model-facing\n * `web_search`/`web_fetch` tools (from `dsh-tool-web`) execute through this.\n * The provider contracts are restated structurally (no dsh-web import) so the\n * plugin resolves outside the monorepo, following the better-sidebar pattern.\n * @module\n */\nimport { classifyFailure, fallbackChain } from \"./fallback.js\";\nimport { resolveSearchChain } from \"./routing-policy.js\";\nimport { buildPool, markUnhealthy, markUsed, reserveKey, releaseKey, selectIndex, PoolEntry } from \"./pool.js\";\nimport { PROVIDERS } from \"./providers/index.js\";\nimport { isKeylessSelfHosted } from \"./providers/types.js\";\nimport { extractSearchHints } from \"./search-hints.js\";\nimport { fetchGenericWebPage, GenericFetchError } from \"./generic-fetch.js\";\n/** Stable provider id registered on ctx.web (the `web` row's searchProvider). */\nexport const PROVIDER_ID = \"dsh-web-tools\";\n/** A classified failure the executor throws (WebError-compatible shape). */\nexport class WebToolsWebError extends Error {\n    code = \"WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR\";\n    attempts;\n}\n/**\n * Shared credential pool store. One instance per plugin; Search and Fetch\n * executors share it so they never fight over separate pools.\n *\n * - Rebuilds a provider's pool ONLY when its credential string changed\n *   (avoids the concurrent-search race of replacing entries out from under an\n *   in-flight request).\n * - Preserves uses/health for keys that persist across rebuilds.\n * - markUsed/markUnhealthy mutate the stable entries array in place.\n */\nexport function createPoolStore(resolveKeys) {\n    const slots = new Map();\n    async function poolOf(providerName) {\n        const raw = await resolveKeys(providerName);\n        const prev = slots.get(providerName);\n        if (prev && prev.raw === raw)\n            return prev.entries;\n        const next = buildPool(raw);\n        if (prev) {\n            const byKey = new Map(prev.entries.map((e) => [e.key, e]));\n            for (const e of next) {\n                const old = byKey.get(e.key);\n                if (old) {\n                    e.uses = old.uses;\n                    e.healthy = old.healthy;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        slots.set(providerName, { raw, entries: next });\n        return next;\n    }\n    /**\n     * Drop one source's pool entirely.\n     *\n     * Used when a source is deleted or its credential/endpoint identity changes:\n     * the cached entries (and any per-key health they carry) no longer describe\n     * anything real. Other sources' pools are untouched.\n     */\n    function forget(providerName) {\n        slots.delete(providerName);\n    }\n    return { poolOf, forget };\n}\n/** Build a WebToolsSearchProvider for `ctx.web.registerSearchProvider`.\n *  `adapterRegistry` is injectable for tests; production uses the global\n *  PROVIDERS map (passed by index.ts via the default).\n *\n *  `resolveSnapshot` is the Issue #9 seam: when supplied, EVERY request reads\n *  one immutable catalog snapshot up front and takes adapters, credentials,\n *  endpoint overrides and keyless-ness from it. A config edit mid-flight can\n *  therefore never swap an adapter out from under the request. */\nexport function createSearchProvider(resolveConfig, resolveKeys, stats, adapterRegistry = PROVIDERS, poolStore, healthStore, resolveSnapshot) {\n    const pools = poolStore ?? createPoolStore(resolveKeys);\n    const routingState = { nextRoundRobinIndex: 0 };\n    /** Adapter for one source id, preferring the live snapshot. */\n    const adapterFor = (sourceId, snapshot) => {\n        if (snapshot)\n            return snapshot.get(sourceId)?.adapter;\n        return adapterRegistry[sourceId];\n    };\n    /** Whether one source can run without a credential. */\n    const keylessOf = (sourceId, adapter, snapshot) => {\n        const entry = snapshot?.get(sourceId);\n        if (entry)\n            return entry.keyless;\n        return isKeylessSelfHosted(adapter);\n    };\n    return {\n        id: PROVIDER_ID,\n        /**\n         * \"Web Search provider service available\": the plugin is enabled AND the\n         * configured chain contains at least one enabled adapter. This deliberately\n         * does NOT check that an API key is configured — keys are resolved lazily\n         * per search and a missing key surfaces as an auth failure at call time.\n         * UI copy treats this as \"service available\" (a chain provider exists), not\n         * \"a credential is ready\"; per-key readiness is shown in the settings card.\n         */\n        available() {\n            const cfg = resolveConfig();\n            if (!cfg.enabled)\n                return false;\n            const snapshot = resolveSnapshot?.();\n            const baseChain = fallbackChain({\n                defaultProvider: cfg.defaultProvider,\n                fallbackOrder: cfg.fallbackOrder,\n            });\n            const chain = resolveSearchChain(baseChain, cfg.searchRoutingPolicy ?? \"ordered\");\n            return chain.some((name) => {\n                if (cfg.enabledProviders[name] === false)\n                    return false;\n                const entry = snapshot?.get(name);\n                if (entry?.config && entry.config.enabled === false)\n                    return false;\n                return adapterFor(name, snapshot) !== undefined;\n            });\n        },\n        async search(request, signal) {\n            const cfg = resolveConfig();\n            if (!cfg.enabled)\n                throw new WebToolsWebError(\"web search is disabled\");\n            // ONE snapshot for the whole request (see the doc comment above).\n            const snapshot = resolveSnapshot?.();\n            // maxResults is owned by the DSH tool layer (it always passes its own);\n            // the plugin does not override it.\n            const maxResults = request.maxResults;\n            const baseChain = fallbackChain({\n                defaultProvider: cfg.defaultProvider,\n                fallbackOrder: cfg.fallbackOrder,\n            });\n            const chain = resolveSearchChain(baseChain, cfg.searchRoutingPolicy ?? \"ordered\", routingState);\n            const attempts = [];\n            let lastError;\n            const searchHints = extractSearchHints(request.query);\n            for (const providerName of chain) {\n                if (cfg.enabledProviders[providerName] === false)\n                    continue;\n                const entryInfo = snapshot?.get(providerName);\n                if (entryInfo?.config && entryInfo.config.enabled === false) {\n                    attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"skipped-disabled\" });\n                    continue;\n                }\n                const adapter = adapterFor(providerName, snapshot);\n                if (!adapter) {\n                    attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"skipped-no-adapter\" });\n                    continue;\n                }\n                let entries = await pools.poolOf(providerName);\n                const keyless = keylessOf(providerName, adapter, snapshot);\n                if (entries.length === 0 && keyless) {\n                    // Keyless sources (self-hosted SearXNG, or a custom source with auth\n                    // mode \"none\") execute with an empty key.\n                    entries = [new PoolEntry(\"\", 0)];\n                }\n                else if (entries.length === 0) {\n                    attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"skipped-no-keys\" });\n                    continue;\n                }\n                // Auth-invalid keys stay unhealthy until the credential actually\n                // changes (refreshPool preserves healthy=false for persisted keys).\n                // If the whole pool is unusable, skip this provider — do NOT reset.\n                let usable = entries.filter((e) => e.healthy);\n                if (usable.length === 0) {\n                    attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"skipped-no-healthy-keys\" });\n                    continue;\n                }\n                // Provider-level cooldown (Retry-After). The store uses its own clock\n                // (injectable for tests) — zero HTTP when cooling down.\n                if (healthStore?.isCoolingDown(providerName)) {\n                    attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"skipped-cooldown\" });\n                    continue;\n                }\n                // Provider-internal key failover: on AUTH failures only, try the next\n                // healthy key in the SAME provider before falling back to another\n                // provider. Non-auth failures (429/5xx/network/timeout) do not rotate\n                // keys — they fall through to the next provider directly.\n                let providerLevelDecision = null;\n                // Base URL from the request snapshot, so an override edit mid-request\n                // cannot make one attempt dial a different host than another.\n                const searchBaseUrl = entryInfo?.builtIn\n                    ? entryInfo.endpoint?.effectiveBaseUrl\n                    : cfg.providerBaseUrls[providerName];\n                while (usable.length > 0) {\n                    const index = selectIndex(entries);\n                    const entry = entries[index];\n                    if (entry)\n                        reserveKey(entries, index);\n                    const started = Date.now();\n                    const providerOptions = cfg.providerOptions?.[providerName];\n                    try {\n                        const outcome = await runWithTimeout((s) => adapter.search(request.query, maxResults, entry?.key ?? \"\", searchBaseUrl, {\n                            signal: s,\n                            options: providerOptions,\n                            hints: searchHints,\n                        }), cfg.providerAttemptTimeoutMs, signal);\n                        if (entry)\n                            markUsed(entries, index);\n                        const latencyMs = Date.now() - started;\n                        attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"success\", latencyMs });\n                        stats.record({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"success\", latencyMs });\n                        return {\n                            ...outcome,\n                            truncated: false,\n                            attempts,\n                            backend: providerName,\n                        };\n                    }\n                    catch (error) {\n                        const err = toProviderError(error);\n                        const latencyMs = Date.now() - started;\n                        const decision = classifyFailure(err);\n                        // Caller cancellation terminates the whole chain — never fall back.\n                        if (decision === \"terminal\") {\n                            providerLevelDecision = \"terminal\";\n                            lastError = err;\n                            attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                            stats.record({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                            break;\n                        }\n                        if (decision === \"non-retryable\") {\n                            providerLevelDecision = \"break\";\n                            lastError = err;\n                            attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                            stats.record({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                            break;\n                        }\n                        // retryable:\n                        if (err.code === \"auth\") {\n                            // key indicted → mark unhealthy, try the next key in this pool\n                            markUnhealthy(entries, index);\n                            attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                            stats.record({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                            usable = entries.filter((e) => e.healthy);\n                            continue;\n                        }\n                        // non-auth retryable (429/5xx/network/timeout) → next provider\n                        lastError = err;\n                        // Only rate-limit errors carry a server-requested cooldown.\n                        if (err.code === \"rate-limit\" && typeof err.retryAfterMs === \"number\" && err.retryAfterMs > 0) {\n                            healthStore?.cooldownFor(providerName, err.retryAfterMs, \"rate-limit\");\n                        }\n                        attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                        stats.record({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}`, latencyMs });\n                        providerLevelDecision = \"next-provider\";\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    finally {\n                        if (entry)\n                            releaseKey(entries, index);\n                    }\n                }\n                if (providerLevelDecision === \"terminal\")\n                    throw toWebError(lastError);\n                if (providerLevelDecision === \"break\")\n                    break;\n                // else fall through to the next provider in the chain\n            }\n            const reason = lastError\n                ? `${lastError.code}: ${lastError.message}`\n                : \"no usable provider\";\n            const err = new WebToolsWebError(`web search failed after ${attempts.length} attempt(s): ${reason}`);\n            err.attempts = attempts;\n            throw err;\n        },\n    };\n}\n/**\n * Build a `WebFetchProvider` for `ctx.web.registerFetchProvider`.\n * Routes fetch through configured native fetch providers (Tavily, Exa, Jina,\n * Firecrawl, Parallel) when available/healthy, and deterministically falls\n * back to the built-in generic HTTP fetcher (with SSRF guard + Defuddle Markdown\n * parsing) when native providers are unavailable, keyless, or fail.\n */\nexport function createFetchProvider(resolveConfig, resolveKeys, adapterRegistry = PROVIDERS, poolStore, healthStore, genericFetcher = fetchGenericWebPage, resolveSnapshot) {\n    const pools = poolStore ?? createPoolStore(resolveKeys);\n    return {\n        id: `${PROVIDER_ID}-fetch`,\n        available() {\n            const cfg = resolveConfig();\n            // Built-in generic fetcher is always available as long as dsh-web-tools is enabled.\n            return cfg.enabled;\n        },\n        async fetch(request, signal) {\n            const cfg = resolveConfig();\n            const snapshot = resolveSnapshot?.();\n            const chain = fallbackChain({\n                defaultProvider: cfg.defaultProvider,\n                fallbackOrder: cfg.fallbackOrder,\n            });\n            const attempts = [];\n            let lastNativeError;\n            void lastNativeError; // retained for debugging inspection if native chain fails\n            // 1. Attempt native fetch from configured, enabled, fetch-capable providers\n            for (const providerName of chain) {\n                if (cfg.enabledProviders[providerName] === false)\n                    continue;\n                const nativeEntry = snapshot?.get(providerName);\n                if (nativeEntry?.config && nativeEntry.config.enabled === false)\n                    continue;\n                const adapter = nativeEntry?.adapter ?? adapterRegistry[providerName];\n                // Custom sources are search-only (fetchCapable=false), so they are\n                // skipped here by construction and page fetching keeps using the\n                // built-in generic fetcher below.\n                if (!adapter || !adapter.fetchCapable)\n                    continue; // not a native fetch backend, skip\n                const entries = await pools.poolOf(providerName);\n                if (entries.length === 0)\n                    continue; // no credentials for this backend\n                const usable = entries.filter((e) => e.healthy);\n                if (usable.length === 0)\n                    continue; // all keys auth-unhealthy, skip provider\n                // Provider cooldown (Retry-After): skip without HTTP call.\n                if (healthStore?.isCoolingDown(providerName))\n                    continue;\n                const index = selectIndex(entries);\n                const entry = entries[index];\n                if (entry)\n                    reserveKey(entries, index);\n                const providerOptions = cfg.providerOptions?.[providerName];\n                // Native fetch endpoints stay on the official host: the base-URL\n                // override applies to SEARCH only (see endpoints.ts), because a gateway\n                // that proxies search may not proxy extraction.\n                const fetchBaseUrl = cfg.providerBaseUrls[providerName];\n                try {\n                    const { text } = await runWithTimeout((sig) => adapter.fetch(request.url, entry?.key ?? \"\", fetchBaseUrl, {\n                        signal: sig,\n                        options: providerOptions,\n                    }), cfg.providerAttemptTimeoutMs, signal);\n                    if (entry)\n                        markUsed(entries, index);\n                    attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: \"success\" });\n                    return {\n                        url: request.url,\n                        statusCode: 200,\n                        body: { kind: \"text\", content: text },\n                        truncated: false,\n                        backend: providerName,\n                    };\n                }\n                catch (error) {\n                    const err = toProviderError(error);\n                    if (err.code === \"auth\")\n                        markUnhealthy(entries, index);\n                    if (err.code === \"rate-limit\" && typeof err.retryAfterMs === \"number\" && err.retryAfterMs > 0) {\n                        healthStore?.cooldownFor(providerName, err.retryAfterMs, \"rate-limit\");\n                    }\n                    lastNativeError = err;\n                    attempts.push({ provider: providerName, outcome: `failed:${err.code}` });\n                    const decision = classifyFailure(err);\n                    // Caller cancellation or terminal URL/SSRF errors should abort immediately without fallback\n                    if (decision === \"terminal\") {\n                        const terminalErr = toWebError(error);\n                        terminalErr.attempts = attempts;\n                        throw terminalErr;\n                    }\n                    if (decision === \"non-retryable\")\n                        break;\n                    // retryable → try next fetch-capable provider in the chain\n                }\n                finally {\n                    if (entry)\n                        releaseKey(entries, index);\n                }\n            }\n            // If caller aborted, do not proceed to built-in generic fetch\n            if (signal?.aborted) {\n                const abortErr = new WebToolsWebError(\"web fetch aborted by caller\");\n                abortErr.code = \"WEB_ABORTED\";\n                abortErr.attempts = attempts;\n                throw abortErr;\n            }\n            // 2. Fallback to built-in generic HTTP fetcher (Defuddle + linkedom)\n            try {\n                const res = await genericFetcher(request.url, {\n                    signal,\n                    timeoutMs: cfg.providerAttemptTimeoutMs,\n                });\n                attempts.push({ provider: \"builtin-http\", outcome: \"success\" });\n                return {\n                    url: res.finalUrl,\n                    statusCode: res.statusCode,\n                    body: { kind: \"text\", content: res.content },\n                    truncated: res.truncated,\n                    backend: res.backend,\n                    metadata: {\n                        title: res.title,\n                        author: res.author,\n                        publishedAt: res.publishedAt,\n                        description: res.description,\n                    },\n                };\n            }\n            catch (genErr) {\n                if (genErr instanceof GenericFetchError) {\n                    attempts.push({ provider: \"builtin-http\", outcome: `failed:${genErr.code}` });\n                    const webErr = new WebToolsWebError(`web fetch failed: ${genErr.message}`);\n                    webErr.code = genErr.code;\n                    webErr.attempts = attempts;\n                    throw webErr;\n                }\n                const fallbackErr = new WebToolsWebError(`web fetch failed: ${genErr instanceof Error ? genErr.message : String(genErr)}`);\n                fallbackErr.attempts = attempts;\n                throw fallbackErr;\n            }\n        },\n    };\n}\n/** Convert any thrown value into a classified ProviderError. */\nfunction toProviderError(error) {\n    if (typeof error === \"object\" && error !== null && \"code\" in error && typeof error.code === \"string\") {\n        return error;\n    }\n    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    const err = new Error(message);\n    err.code = \"network\";\n    return err;\n}\n/** Wrap an unknown failure from a provider call into a WebToolsWebError. */\nfunction toWebError(error) {\n    const p = toProviderError(error);\n    const err = new WebToolsWebError(p.message);\n    // preserve cancellation semantics: aborted stays aborted\n    if (p.code === \"aborted\")\n        err.code = \"WEB_ABORTED\";\n    return err;\n}\n/**\n * Run a provider attempt with a real abort: the provider's fetch receives a\n * signal that fires on EITHER the caller's cancellation OR this attempt's\n * timeout, so a timeout genuinely aborts the in-flight HTTP request (no\n * background request lingering / burning quota).\n *\n * Distinguishes the two cases:\n *  - caller abort  → rejects with `aborted` (terminal; the chain stops)\n *  - attempt timeout → rejects with `timeout` (retryable; fallback proceeds)\n *\n * @param run - the provider call; receives the merged abort signal.\n * @param timeoutMs - per-attempt budget; <=0 disables the timer.\n * @param externalSignal - the caller's AbortSignal (optional).\n */\nasync function runWithTimeout(run, timeoutMs, externalSignal) {\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    // Explicit abort-cause state. A caller abort CLEARS the timer immediately,\n    // so a late timer callback can never flip a caller cancellation into a\n    // timeout (which would wrongly trigger fallback).\n    let abortCause;\n    let timer;\n    const clearTimer = () => {\n        if (timer) {\n            clearTimeout(timer);\n            timer = undefined;\n        }\n    };\n    const onExternalAbort = () => {\n        abortCause = \"caller\";\n        clearTimer();\n        controller.abort(externalSignal?.reason);\n    };\n    if (externalSignal) {\n        if (externalSignal.aborted)\n            throw providerErrorOf(\"aborted\", \"search aborted by caller\");\n        externalSignal.addEventListener(\"abort\", onExternalAbort, { once: true });\n    }\n    if (Number.isFinite(timeoutMs) && timeoutMs > 0) {\n        timer = setTimeout(() => {\n            if (abortCause !== undefined)\n                return; // already aborted by caller\n            abortCause = \"timeout\";\n            controller.abort(new Error(`provider timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`));\n        }, timeoutMs);\n    }\n    try {\n        const value = await run(controller.signal);\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) {\n            throw providerErrorOf(abortCause === \"timeout\" ? \"timeout\" : \"aborted\", controller.signal.reason?.message ?? \"attempt aborted\");\n        }\n        return value;\n    }\n    catch (error) {\n        // If OUR timer fired, the provider's own abort (whatever code it raised)\n        // is a TIMEOUT — even if the adapter rethrew its own 'aborted'. External\n        // cancellation is only 'aborted' when abortCause is not \"timeout\".\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) {\n            throw providerErrorOf(abortCause === \"timeout\" ? \"timeout\" : \"aborted\", controller.signal.reason instanceof Error ? controller.signal.reason.message : String(controller.signal.reason ?? \"aborted\"));\n        }\n        throw error;\n    }\n    finally {\n        clearTimer();\n        if (externalSignal)\n            externalSignal.removeEventListener(\"abort\", onExternalAbort);\n    }\n}\n/** Build a classified ProviderError with a code + message. */\nfunction providerErrorOf(code, message) {\n    const err = new Error(message);\n    err.code = code;\n    return err;\n}\n"

      "path": "lib/host/pool.js",
      "content": "/**\n * dsh-web-tools — per-provider account pool (pure logic, no I/O).\n *\n * Each provider can hold a pool of API keys (e.g. several Tavily accounts).\n * Selection policy: least-used-first with a fixed tie-break order (the key\n * list order). A key that fails a call is marked unhealthy and skipped until\n * the whole pool is exhausted, at which point health resets so a recovered\n * account can be used again.\n *\n * This serves legitimate multi-key / rollover / load-spreading scenarios only.\n * @module\n */\n/** One key's live state inside a provider pool. */\nexport class PoolEntry {\n    key;\n    order;\n    /** Active concurrent requests currently using this key. */\n    inFlight = 0;\n    /** Searches dispatched through this key so far. */\n    uses = 0;\n    /** False after a failed call; skipped by selection until a full reset. */\n    healthy = true;\n    constructor(key, order) {\n        this.key = key;\n        this.order = order;\n    }\n}\n/**\n * Short diagnostic hint: provider-known prefix (e.g. \"tvly\") + last 4 chars.\n * Deliberately NOT the first 9 chars of the raw key — enough to identify a\n * key without revealing a significant secret prefix.\n */\nexport function hintOf(key) {\n    const prefix = key.slice(0, key.indexOf(\"-\") > 0 ? key.indexOf(\"-\") : 4);\n    const tail = key.length > 6 ? key.slice(-4) : key;\n    return `${prefix}-…${tail}`;\n}\n/**\n * Select the next key index: among healthy entries, lowest inFlight first,\n * then fewest total uses; ties broken by fixed `order`. Deterministic & concurrency-aware.\n * @param entries\n * @returns index into `entries`.\n * @throws {Error} empty pool or no healthy key.\n */\nexport function selectIndex(entries) {\n    if (entries.length === 0)\n        throw new Error(\"provider pool is empty\");\n    const usable = entries.filter((e) => e.healthy);\n    if (usable.length === 0)\n        throw new Error(\"provider pool has no healthy keys left\");\n    let best = usable[0];\n    for (const e of usable) {\n        if (e.inFlight < best.inFlight ||\n            (e.inFlight === best.inFlight && e.uses < best.uses) ||\n            (e.inFlight === best.inFlight && e.uses === best.uses && e.order < best.order)) {\n            best = e;\n        }\n    }\n    return entries.indexOf(best);\n}\n/** Reserve one dispatch slot through `index` (increments inFlight). */\nexport function reserveKey(entries, index) {\n    if (entries[index]) {\n        entries[index].inFlight += 1;\n    }\n}\n/** Release one dispatch slot through `index` (decrements inFlight). */\nexport function releaseKey(entries, index) {\n    if (entries[index]) {\n        entries[index].inFlight = Math.max(0, entries[index].inFlight - 1);\n    }\n}\n/** Record one successful dispatch through `index`. */\nexport function markUsed(entries, index) {\n    if (entries[index]) {\n        entries[index].uses += 1;\n    }\n}\n/** Record one failed dispatch through `index`. */\nexport function markUnhealthy(entries, index) {\n    if (entries[index]) {\n        entries[index].healthy = false;\n    }\n}\n/** Reset every entry to healthy (called when the whole pool is exhausted). */\nexport function resetHealth(entries) {\n    for (const e of entries)\n        e.healthy = true;\n}\n/**\n * Build pool entries from a configured key string.\n * Accepted separators: comma, whitespace/newline, or semicolon.\n * Duplicate keys are dropped (first occurrence keeps its order).\n * Empty input → empty pool (provider effectively unconfigured).\n * @param raw configured credential value.\n * @returns PoolEntry[]\n */\nexport function buildPool(raw) {\n    const parts = (raw ?? \"\").split(/[,\\s;]+/).map((s) => s.trim()).filter((s) => s.length > 0);\n    const seen = new Set();\n    const entries = [];\n    for (const key of parts) {\n        if (seen.has(key))\n            continue;\n        seen.add(key);\n        entries.push(new PoolEntry(key, entries.length));\n    }\n    return entries;\n}\n/** Pool summary for diagnostics (no secrets). */\nexport function poolSummary(entries) {\n    return entries.map((e) => ({ hint: hintOf(e.key), uses: e.uses, healthy: e.healthy }));\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "lib/host/fallback.js",
      "content": "/**\n * dsh-web-tools — deterministic fallback policy (pure logic).\n *\n * Retryable failures trigger fallback to the next provider in order:\n *   429 (rate limit), 408 (timeout), 5xx, network unavailable, provider\n *   unavailable, caller timeout, AND auth failures (401/403): a bad key on\n *   one provider should not block the user's search — the key is marked\n *   unhealthy and the UI shows an auth error, but the search continues.\n * Non-retryable (never fall back): 400 invalid query, schema/config bugs,\n * programming errors — silently switching would hide broken configuration.\n * Terminal: caller cancellation (aborted) — the whole chain must stop\n * immediately, never continue to the next provider.\n * @module\n */\n/** Error kinds the fallback treats as retryable. */\nexport const RETRYABLE = new Set([\"rate-limit\", \"timeout\", \"server\", \"network\", \"unavailable\", \"auth\"]);\n/** Error kinds that never trigger fallback. */\nexport const NON_RETRYABLE = new Set([\"bad-request\", \"config\"]);\n/** Error kinds that terminate the whole chain (caller cancellation). */\nexport const TERMINAL = new Set([\"aborted\"]);\n/**\n * Classify a provider failure.\n * @param opts\n * @param opts.code machine code from the provider adapter.\n * @returns {\"retryable\"|\"non-retryable\"|\"terminal\"}\n */\nexport function classifyFailure(opts) {\n    const { code } = opts;\n    if (TERMINAL.has(code))\n        return \"terminal\";\n    if (RETRYABLE.has(code))\n        return \"retryable\";\n    if (NON_RETRYABLE.has(code))\n        return \"non-retryable\";\n    // unknown codes are treated as retryable (conservative: try the next provider)\n    return \"retryable\";\n}\n/**\n * Compute the fallback chain for one operation: the default provider first,\n * then every configured fallback entry in order (deduped). No artificial cap —\n * the user configures the chain; total time is bounded by the attempt timeout\n * and the DSH tool-level timeout.\n */\nexport function fallbackChain(opts) {\n    const { defaultProvider, fallbackOrder } = opts;\n    const chain = [defaultProvider];\n    const seen = new Set(chain);\n    for (const name of fallbackOrder ?? []) {\n        if (seen.has(name))\n            continue;\n        seen.add(name);\n        chain.push(name);\n    }\n    return chain;\n}\n/**\n * Deterministic decision record for one search attempt.\n */\nexport function attemptRecord(opts) {\n    const { provider, attempt, outcome, latencyMs } = opts;\n    return {\n        provider,\n        attempt,\n        outcome,\n        ...(latencyMs !== undefined ? { latencyMs } : {}),\n    };\n}\n"
    },

      "content": "/**\n * dsh-web-tools — SearchHints semantic extraction layer.\n *\n * Deterministic, zero-LLM lightweight semantic extraction from user queries.\n * Extracts high-confidence hints:\n *  - topic: \"code\" | \"news\" | \"finance\" | \"research\" | \"general\"\n *  - freshness: preset (\"day\" | \"week\" | \"month\" | \"year\"), after_date (YYYY-MM-DD), before_date\n *  - domains: include (hard filter, e.g. site:github.com), exclude (-site:), prefer (soft preference, e.g. \"官方文档/official docs\")\n *  - locale: language, country\n *  - cleanQuery: query with syntax operators (site:, -site:) stripped for pure keyword matching\n *\n * Principle: ONLY explicit constraints become hard filters (include/exclude domains).\n * Soft preferences (preferDomains / official sources) steer the objective rather than killing recall.\n * @module\n */\n/**\n * Format a Date object to YYYY-MM-DD\n */\nexport function formatDateYMD(d) {\n    const year = d.getUTCFullYear();\n    const month = String(d.getUTCMonth() + 1).padStart(2, \"0\");\n    const day = String(d.getUTCDate()).padStart(2, \"0\");\n    return `${year}-${month}-${day}`;\n}\n/**\n * Calculate an after_date string from a preset relative to a reference date.\n */\nexport function calculateAfterDate(preset, now = new Date()) {\n    const d = new Date(now.getTime());\n    switch (preset) {\n        case \"day\":\n            d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() - 1);\n            break;\n        case \"week\":\n            d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() - 7);\n            break;\n        case \"month\":\n            d.setUTCMonth(d.getUTCMonth() - 1);\n            break;\n        case \"year\":\n            d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1);\n            break;\n    }\n    return formatDateYMD(d);\n}\n// Regex patterns for operator extraction\nconst SITE_INCLUDE_RE = /(?:^|\\s)site:([a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})(?:\\b|\\s|$)/gi;\nconst SITE_EXCLUDE_RE = /(?:^|\\s)-site:([a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})(?:\\b|\\s|$)/gi;\n// Platform indicators (high precision to avoid false positives on solitary 'x' or common words)\nconst XIAOHONGSHU_EXPLICIT_RE = /(?:小红书|rednote|\\bxsec_token\\b)/i;\nconst XIAOHONGSHU_CLEAN_RE = /(?:(?:请\\s*)?(?:在|去)?\\s*(?:小红书|rednote)(?:上|里|中)?\\s*(?:搜索|搜|查找|找|看看)?)/gi;\nconst X_EXPLICIT_RE = /(?:twitter|推特|x\\.com|twitter\\.com|(?:在|上)X(?:上|里|中)?|X\\s*(?:平台|推特|社区|帖子|动态|热搜)|^\\s*X\\s*[:：])/i;\nconst X_ROUTE_PREFIX_RE = /^\\s*X\\s*[:：]\\s*/i;\nconst X_CLEAN_RE = /(?:(?:请\\s*)?(?:在|去)?\\s*(?:X(?:上|里|中)|(?:twitter|推特)(?:上|里|中)?|X\\s*(?:平台|推特|社区|帖子|动态|热搜)(?:上|里|中)?)\\s*(?:搜索|搜|查找|找|看看)?)/gi;\n// Code topic indicators (keywords or patterns)\nconst CODE_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(github|gitlab|npm|pnpm|cargo|pip|pypi|nuget|crates\\.io|stackoverflow|golang|typescript|python|rust|c\\+\\+|javascript|react|vue|svelte|docker|k8s|kubernetes|linux|bash|powershell|sql|postgres|redis|git|api|sdk|graphql|rest|grpc|webhook|bug|error|issue|pr|pull request|stacktrace|exception|panic|segfault|syntax|compiler|traceback)\\b/i,\n    /(?:代码|函数|接口|报错|崩溃|源码|组件|配置|版本号|仓库|提交|异常|编译)/,\n];\n// News topic indicators\nconst NEWS_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(news|breaking|announced|announcement|press release|headline|journal|report|coverage)\\b/i,\n    /(?:新闻|快讯|发布会|报道|最新消息|突发|动态|头条)/,\n];\n// Finance topic indicators\nconst FINANCE_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(stock|shares|nasdaq|nyse|sec|10-k|10-q|earnings|revenue|market cap|valuation|ipo|crypto|bitcoin|ethereum|dividend|fiscal|quarterly|ebitda)\\b/i,\n    /(?:财报|股价|营收|市值|估值|财季|分红|股票|证券|上市|收益率|净利润)/,\n];\n// Research topic indicators\nconst RESEARCH_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(arxiv|paper|research|benchmark|ablation|evaluation|dataset|methodology|conference|neurips|icml|iclr|cvpr|acl|ieee|springer|nature|science)\\b/i,\n    /(?:论文|学术|评测|基准|消融实验|数据集|学术会议|研报|文献)/,\n];\n// Freshness indicators\nconst DAY_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(today|past 24 hours|last 24 hours|24h|today's)\\b/i,\n    /(?:今天|今日|过去24小时|24小时内|当天)/,\n];\nconst WEEK_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(this week|past week|last 7 days|7d|recent week)\\b/i,\n    /(?:本周|这一周|过去7天|近7天|最近一周)/,\n];\nconst MONTH_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(this month|past month|last 30 days|latest|recently|recent|newest|current)\\b/i,\n    /(?:本月|过去30天|近1个月|最近|最新|近期|近来)/,\n];\nconst YEAR_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(this year|past year|last 12 months|annual)\\b/i,\n    /(?:今年|本年度|近1年|过去一年)/,\n];\n// Explicit date range in query (e.g. 2026-08-01..2026-08-20 or after:2026-01-01)\nconst AFTER_DATE_RE = /\\bafter:(\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2})\\b/i;\nconst BEFORE_DATE_RE = /\\bbefore:(\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2})\\b/i;\n// Official source preference indicators\nconst OFFICIAL_PREFERENCE_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(official|primary doc|primary documentation|official docs?|official website|canonical source)\\b/i,\n    /(?:官方文档|官网|官方|权威来源|正规文档|官方指南)/,\n];\n// Multi-country / Global suppressors: when user specifies multiple countries or global terms, avoid biasing to a single country.\nconst GLOBAL_SCOPE_INDICATORS = [\n    /\\b(international|worldwide|global|globally)\\b/i,\n    /(?:国内外|海内外|全球|世界范围|跨国|国际)/,\n];\n// Country indicators (only assign country when explicitly mentioned in the query)\nconst EXPLICIT_COUNTRY_PATTERNS = [\n    { re: /(?:美国|美股|美联储|United States|USA|\\bUS\\b)/i, country: \"US\" },\n    { re: /(?:中国|国内|A股|China|\\bCN\\b)/i, country: \"CN\" },\n    { re: /(?:日本|日经|Japan|\\bJP\\b)/i, country: \"JP\" },\n    { re: /(?:英国|United Kingdom|\\bUK\\b|\\bGB\\b)/i, country: \"GB\" },\n    { re: /(?:新加坡|Singapore|\\bSG\\b)/i, country: \"SG\" },\n    { re: /(?:德国|Germany|\\bDE\\b)/i, country: \"DE\" },\n    { re: /(?:法国|France|\\bFR\\b)/i, country: \"FR\" },\n    { re: /(?:加拿大|Canada|\\bCA\\b)/i, country: \"CA\" },\n];\n/**\n * Extract structured SearchHints from a raw query.\n * Pure function: deterministic, fast, testable, zero side-effects.\n */\nexport function extractSearchHints(query, now = new Date()) {\n    const rawQuery = (query ?? \"\").trim();\n    let cleanQuery = rawQuery;\n    // 1. Extract domain include/exclude\n    const includeDomains = [];\n    const excludeDomains = [];\n    let match;\n    // Extract -site:\n    const excludeRe = new RegExp(SITE_EXCLUDE_RE.source, \"gi\");\n    while ((match = excludeRe.exec(rawQuery)) !== null) {\n        const domain = match[1]?.toLowerCase();\n        if (domain && !excludeDomains.includes(domain)) {\n            excludeDomains.push(domain);\n        }\n    }\n    cleanQuery = cleanQuery.replace(SITE_EXCLUDE_RE, \" \");\n    // Extract site:\n    const includeRe = new RegExp(SITE_INCLUDE_RE.source, \"gi\");\n    while ((match = includeRe.exec(rawQuery)) !== null) {\n        const domain = match[1]?.toLowerCase();\n        if (domain && !includeDomains.includes(domain)) {\n            includeDomains.push(domain);\n        }\n    }\n    cleanQuery = cleanQuery.replace(SITE_INCLUDE_RE, \" \");\n    // 1.1 Extract Platform Hint (Xiaohongshu vs X/Twitter)\n    let platform;\n    let platformExplicit = false;\n    const isXhsDomain = includeDomains.some((d) => d.includes(\"xiaohongshu.com\") || d.includes(\"xhslink.com\"));\n    const isXDomain = includeDomains.some((d) => d.includes(\"x.com\") || d.includes(\"twitter.com\"));\n    if (isXhsDomain || XIAOHONGSHU_EXPLICIT_RE.test(rawQuery)) {\n        platform = \"xiaohongshu\";\n        platformExplicit = true;\n        cleanQuery = cleanQuery.replace(XIAOHONGSHU_CLEAN_RE, \" \");\n    }\n    else if (isXDomain || X_EXPLICIT_RE.test(rawQuery)) {\n        platform = \"x\";\n        platformExplicit = true;\n        cleanQuery = cleanQuery.replace(X_ROUTE_PREFIX_RE, \" \").replace(X_CLEAN_RE, \" \");\n    }\n    // 2. Extract explicit after: / before: dates\n    let afterDate;\n    let beforeDate;\n    const afterMatch = AFTER_DATE_RE.exec(cleanQuery);\n    if (afterMatch) {\n        afterDate = afterMatch[1];\n        cleanQuery = cleanQuery.replace(AFTER_DATE_RE, \" \");\n    }\n    const beforeMatch = BEFORE_DATE_RE.exec(cleanQuery);\n    if (beforeMatch) {\n        beforeDate = beforeMatch[1];\n        cleanQuery = cleanQuery.replace(BEFORE_DATE_RE, \" \");\n    }\n    // 3. Topic classification (needed before freshness rules to avoid over-constraining evergreen technical queries)\n    let topic = \"general\";\n    if (includeDomains.some((d) => d.includes(\"github.com\") || d.includes(\"gitlab.com\") || d.includes(\"stackoverflow.com\")) ||\n        CODE_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n        topic = \"code\";\n    }\n    else if (includeDomains.some((d) => d.includes(\"arxiv.org\")) ||\n        RESEARCH_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n        topic = \"research\";\n    }\n    else if (FINANCE_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n        topic = \"finance\";\n    }\n    else if (NEWS_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n        topic = \"news\";\n    }\n    // 4. Extract freshness preset:\n    // Hard freshness (day/week): applied across all topics.\n    // Soft freshness (month/year keywords like latest/recent/current): applied ONLY if topic === \"news\"\n    // or when explicit after/before is given, to avoid truncating evergreen docs like \"latest React docs\".\n    let freshnessPreset;\n    if (!afterDate && !beforeDate) {\n        if (DAY_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n            freshnessPreset = \"day\";\n        }\n        else if (WEEK_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n            freshnessPreset = \"week\";\n        }\n        else if (topic === \"news\" && MONTH_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n            freshnessPreset = \"month\";\n        }\n        else if (topic === \"news\" && YEAR_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery))) {\n            freshnessPreset = \"year\";\n        }\n    }\n    const freshness = freshnessPreset || afterDate || beforeDate\n        ? {\n            preset: freshnessPreset,\n            after: afterDate ?? (freshnessPreset ? calculateAfterDate(freshnessPreset, now) : undefined),\n            before: beforeDate,\n        }\n        : undefined;\n    // 5. Official / Prefer domains\n    const preferOfficial = OFFICIAL_PREFERENCE_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery));\n    const preferDomains = [];\n    if (includeDomains.length > 0) {\n        // If includeDomains is present, it's also a preferred domain\n        preferDomains.push(...includeDomains);\n    }\n    const domains = includeDomains.length > 0 || excludeDomains.length > 0 || preferDomains.length > 0 || preferOfficial\n        ? {\n            include: includeDomains.length > 0 ? includeDomains : undefined,\n            exclude: excludeDomains.length > 0 ? excludeDomains : undefined,\n            prefer: preferDomains.length > 0 ? preferDomains : undefined,\n            preferOfficial,\n        }\n        : undefined;\n    // 6. Locale hint detection (language decoupled from country!)\n    // ONLY set country when explicitly mentioned in query text.\n    let language;\n    const hasChinese = /[\\u4e00-\\u9fa5]/.test(rawQuery);\n    const hasJapanese = /[\\u3040-\\u30ff]/.test(rawQuery);\n    if (hasChinese) {\n        language = \"zh\";\n    }\n    else if (hasJapanese) {\n        language = \"ja\";\n    }\n    let country;\n    const isGlobalScope = GLOBAL_SCOPE_INDICATORS.some((re) => re.test(rawQuery));\n    if (!isGlobalScope) {\n        const matchedCountries = EXPLICIT_COUNTRY_PATTERNS.filter((p) => p.re.test(rawQuery)).map((p) => p.country);\n        const uniqueCountries = [...new Set(matchedCountries)];\n        if (uniqueCountries.length === 1) {\n            country = uniqueCountries[0];\n        }\n    }\n    const locale = language || country ? { language, country } : undefined;\n    // Clean extra whitespaces in cleanQuery\n    cleanQuery = cleanQuery\n        .replace(/^[\\s:：,，;；\\-—]+|[\\s:：,，;；\\-—]+$/g, \" \")\n        .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n        .trim();\n    if (!cleanQuery)\n        cleanQuery = rawQuery;\n    return {\n        topic,\n        platform,\n        platformExplicit: platformExplicit ? true : undefined,\n        freshness,\n        domains,\n        locale,\n        cleanQuery,\n        rawQuery,\n    };\n}\n"
    },
